national.title: California warned of potential Thanksgiving flooding as storms threaten US coasts
national.summary: Parts of the Canadian province of British Columbia may also be affected by the storms, which come as millions of people travel for the holiday.
national.body:
Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday.

Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month.

The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding.

Meanwhile, storms are also forecast for the Pacific Northwest, including the Canadian province of British Columbia, and eastern parts of the US.

Portions of a pier in northern California came crashing down into the ocean on Wednesday as high tides and strong waves battered the structure, video showed.

Beachgoers have been advised to stay away from the water's edge as large waves could suddenly form. Such waves could be damaging to piers and jetties, and could capsize small vessels, the NWS warned.

Flooding has already been reported in the San Francisco Bay Area.

In San Diego, a high tide of 8 ft 11in was recorded on Wednesday morning local time - potentially breaking the record for highest tide measured in the area, which was just set late last month at 7.98ft.

national.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
national.summary: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.
national.body:
The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy.

The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.

The White House began investigating the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal .

China is facing the highest tariff rate of up to 40%, followed by Vietnam at up to 35%, with others facing either 20% or 25%.

The US Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed tariffs together with extensive reports of how each jurisdiction's trade practices purportedly impact American commerce.

The new duties are not expected to take effect until next year and have to go through rounds of public consultation and, potentially, hearings.

Tariffs are taxes levied on imported goods. The amount is typically calculated as a percentage of a good's value and paid to the government by businesses importing products.

Some of these rates will be effectively reduced because of caps on tariffs Trump has agreed to. Individual countries also face different levies.

national.summary: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.
national.body: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday. The 100th annual parade will now kick off Saturday at 8:30 a.m.The historic move comes as a powerful coastal storm is set to impact the area Thursday. "The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our city and agency partners, we've made the decision to move the celebration due to expected severe weather," Macy's said in a statement. "Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.""Created by Macy's colleagues since 1924 as a gift to our city and nation, our parade has brought magic into the hearts of millions and have created cherished memories that have spanned generations," Will Coss, executive producer and vice president of Macy's Branded Entertainment, said at a press conference Wednesday. "This year we marked our 100th march, a milestone built on creativity, celebration and tradition. While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our participants and spectators is and always will be our top priority." "We know that our city is the greatest city in the world, and we also know that in our city, nothing comes easily, and you have to plan for every possibility," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. "And while we were looking forward to celebrating Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow, extreme weather has forced us to reschedule for Saturday instead." Mamdani pointed to the "heavy storm" expected Thursday, with wind gusts up to 65 mph possible, along with potential flash flooding. "Now I know many New Yorkers, myself included as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow," Mamdani said. "I know that this change of plan will cause inconveniences, yet safety has to come first. And on Saturday, when balloons climb into the sky, every New Yorker and everyone visiting, will be able to take in a show that is both truly spectacular and also safe." Democrats had argued the TV spots were illegal government-sponsored propaganda intended to promote the president's campaign message just weeks before November's midterm elections. In her ruling, she noted that a previous temporary restraining order against the ads had been issued when the election was less than a week away."But the November 2026 midterm elections have come and gone," she wrote, adding that the DNC was now claiming the party could be harmed by the ads in December congressional runoff elections or even because the 2028 presidential cycle has already begun."At this juncture and on this record, the court is unpersuaded," AliKhan wrote.Her ruling comes after another judge in a similar case in New York also declined a long-term ban on the ads.The ads first emerged on cable and broadcast networks — including CBS — in late September, just over a month before the midterms, funded by a $20 million Department of Homeland Security contract. national.summary: A crash involving a fuel tanker has ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 31 people.
national.body: A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said. The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the Health Ministry. The stretch of the highway where the crash occurred was in Warraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo area, according to the Health Ministry.At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video shows firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic as the road was blocked after the accident, saw the fuel truck and many cars on fire. He said he saw at least eight bodies being removed from burned cars."It was a huge fire; the cars got stuck together because of the fire," he told the AP, describing the fear and panic that followed. "It was a shocking scene."Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The Public Prosecutor's office said DNA investigations were underway to identify the victims.Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further. Initial statements said 25 people were injured, but that figure was later revised to 21.Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.In January, 21 people were killed and 16 were injured in a massive multicar pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.

national.summary: The U.S. Army detonated a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday, after days of back-and-forth between politicians and the courts.
national.body: The U.S. Army detonated a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday morning, following community outcry and a legal fight over concerns of a possible dust plume containing toxic lead particles spreading after the blast. Five tons of unstable explosive material, containing the highly sensitive compound lead azide, were blown up in a controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, which is a small community of about 350 people, located four hours west of Chicago by car. As scheduled, the detonation took place at 9 a.m. local time. A few loud pops rang out in livestream footage of the explosion published by The Associated Press, followed by a faint smoke cloud that rose up above the rooftop of the Armed Forces Reserve Center building that separated its cameras from the detonation site.Fifteen minutes after it happened, the Environmental Protection Agency reported that zero lead was detected in the air by four monitors stations in the area. Those sensors continued to show the same readings two hours later, according to the EPA. The Army said in a follow-up social media post Wednesday evening that the Federal Emergency Management Agency had given an "all clear" around the plant. The Army also added that maps from the Pentagon's Defense Threat Reduction Agency indicated "ZERO airborne lead detection" from the detonation. FEMA said in a separate statement Wednesday night that its air monitoring results indicated there was "no detectable lead."Army Maj. Gen. Eric P. Shirley, the commander of the operation, described the detonation as "tremendously successful" at a news conference Wednesday."I believe absolutely that we reduced, as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible, the risk to the health and the safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa," he said.Rob Cekada, the director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, added that the operation went "100% as planned," with the blast driving the explosion into the ground and minimizing the the amount of lead dispersed into the atmosphere, as designed.Earlier, local officials told CBS News minutes after the explosion that the smoke plume was visible in Iowa. national.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died at age 65 following a battle with prostate cancer.
national.body: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran — whose huge pop hits included "Hungry Like the Wolf," "The Reflex" and "Rio" — and who were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.Taylor died following a "courageous battle with prostate cancer," his family and the band said in a joint statement posted to social media. He died Monday at his home surrounded by friends and family."To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his family said. On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend."I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band," he wrote at the time. "You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible."His family said Wednesday that Taylor "faced the last few years with so much courage and determination until the very end, never losing his love of life."The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients."Andy was there at the very beginning of our story," the band said in Wednesday's statement. "From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music."The band's 1981 debut album "Duran Duran" had their first hit single, "Planet Earth," but it was "Rio" that transformed them into trans-Atlantic stars. national.title: The US pastor who wants to see women's right to vote overturned
national.summary: The movement to repeal women's right to vote has gained traction amongst some very conservative Christians.
national.body:
"Patriarchy is in accordance with the way God made the world." That is the view of Pastor Doug Wilson, a conservative minister who the US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth calls his mentor.

Speaking to the BBC from his base in Moscow, Idaho, Wilson explained his view that a society led by men is "a very great blessing". It's a perspective Christians who disagree with him say is based on a fundamentalist understanding of the Bible, which promotes the subjugation of women.

A self-described Christian nationalist, Wilson believes the US should be a theocracy, with gay sex criminalised, abortion outlawed, and people of other faiths unable to hold public office.

In the past he has delivered a sermon on "The Lost Virtue of Sexism," arguing that the Bible says women should be excluded from leadership of the church, and certain roles in civic affairs. And as part of his views on the division between the sexes, he would like the 19th Amendment of the US constitution, which granted women the right to vote, to be repealed, something his detractors say is anti-democratic.

The vast majority of Christians support women's right to vote, and dismiss his message as misogynistic and extreme.

Rev. Canon Dana Colley Corsello, the vicar at the Washington National Cathedral, rejects Wilson's understanding of what the Bible says about women's roles.

"In my mind, there is no biblical precedent or standing for what [Wilson has] proposed," she told the BBC.

"I'm married, I have a husband, I have children. My husband and I are complete equals in everything we do."

national.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
national.summary: Despite widespread concern from residents ahead of the blast, officials say that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.
national.body:
The US military has hailed as a "huge success" the detonation of nearly five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa, an operation that sparked fears of health and environmental problems across the region.

Smoke was seen rising into the sky shortly after 09:00 local time (14:00 GMT) following the explosion, as the Army declared the risk "as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible".

Plans to detonate the lead azide, a volatile compound reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were paused several times before the blast following public outcry and legal challenges.

On Wednesday evening, the Army said that an "all clear" has been issued around the ammunition plant.

President Donald Trump said shortly after the blast that reports showed mitigation efforts "far exceeded expectations".

"The Army's controlled, mitigated detonation exceeded all expectations and was a HUGE success," Adam Telle, acting secretary of the US Army, wrote on social media.

Despite widespread concern from residents of Middletown, Iowa, ahead of the blast, officials have said that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.

In a Wednesday evening update on X, the Army said that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema) had issued the "all clear" around the plant and that there was no airborne lead detection following the detonation.

national.title: Spanish elections: What you need to know and what's at stake
national.summary: After eight years of Socialist-led rule, snap elections are taking place on Sunday with conservative Alberto Núñez Feijóo vying to win office.
national.body:
After eight years of Socialist-led government under Pedro Sánchez, Spain is at a crossroads.

Snap elections are taking place on Sunday 29 November, and voters face a choice of continued left-wing rule or a conservative-led government, with the likely support of far-right Vox.

Alberto Núñez Feijóo's conservative People's Party is narrowly ahead of the Socialist PSOE in most polls.

He has spoken of Spain being probably at "the most significant moment in our country for the past 50 years", and he aims to "repair the state, regenerate democracy, reunited the nation and recover Spain's ambition and self-esteem". But it is unlikely he could do anything without the backing of Vox, who are third in the opinion polls.

For more on Feijóo and who else to watch in this election - read here .

Spain has a population of almost 50 million, and almost 39 million people have the right to vote for the Congress and the upper house, the Senate. The polls open at 09:00 (08:00 GMT) on Sunday and close at 20:00 (19:00 GMT), when the first exit polls come out.

Sánchez called this vote eight months early after MPs rejected planned changes to Spain's housing laws.

He was responding to nationwide protests after an 87-year-old woman called Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her rented flat in Madrid and later died.

national.title: France's political mainstream risks presidential vote debacle with no clear candidate
national.summary: Hard-right and hard-left candidates dominate the polls ahead of next year's presidential election.
national.body:
France's political mainstream faces wipe-out at the presidential election in April-May 2027, unless it acts fast to choose who it wishes to stand.

With every poll confirming the dominance of hard-right and hard-left leaders Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, candidates of the middle-ground – the old "legacy" parties – are being squeezed out of the game.

In theory any contender from centre-right or centre-left who was chosen in the first multi-candidate round of voting in April should be in a strong position to win in the play-off a fortnight later.

That is because at their separate ends of the spectrum both Le Pen and Mélenchon have more people who oppose than support them.

But personal rivalries, lack of preparation and differing political visions have so far put paid to any hope of a meaningful challenge.

"The game in the centre is totally blocked," says political writer François Fressoz at the left-leaning Le Monde newspaper. "The partisans of reason have lost their reason."

On the left – the old Socialist Party and its acolytes – there is at least agreement on a candidate: European Parliament MP Raphaël Glucksmann.

His problem is that allies who he might once have counted on – Greens, Communists and other small left-wing parties, not to mention many Socialist voters – are being pulled inexorably into the Mélenchon orbit.

national.title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?
national.summary: Jihadist groups appear to be focusing on local issues rather than global terror. Does it signify a real change?
national.body:
Rice, pasta, sugar, cooking oil and beans are hardly what you'd expect to see in jihadist propaganda. Yet these were among the supplies that al-Qaeda's Somali branch, al-Shabab, said its "charity" had handed out to hundreds of struggling families in August, as it publicised the aid through its social media accounts and radio station.

The group, which controls large parts of rural southern and central Somalia, has been keen to show off its so-called humanitarian work throughout 2026.

"May God reward them," said a local woman in one of al-Shabab's videos.

It's all part of an effort to win over local communities and present itself as more than just a jihadist group.

A quarter of a century after al-Qaeda's 9/11 attacks in the US, and 12 years after Islamic State group (IS) declared its so-called caliphate in Iraq and Syria, the jihadist movement looks very different.

Rather than focusing on attacking the West or fighting for a global Islamic state, some - especially those linked to al-Qaeda - are putting more effort into winning power closer to home. And they seem increasingly willing to make compromises along the way.

Because of this, a debate is growing within the movement. While hardliners reject compromise, pragmatists see working with local groups and former enemies as a way to gain power. But do the pragmatists represent a genuine change or simply a shift in tactics to achieve the same ultimate goals: establishing a state that applies their strict interpretation of Islamic Sharia law both at home and in its dealings with the outside world?

Neither al-Qaeda nor IS has achieved its ultimate dream: taking over one or more countries and ruling them according to their strict interpretation of Islam.

national.title: US approves SpaceX plan to send a million data satellites to space
national.summary: The Starmind constellation aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for AI computing power.
national.body:
US regulators have given SpaceX the go-ahead to launch a million satellites into Earth's orbit to help build data centres in space - the first approval of its kind.

The company, which is owned by Elon Musk, wants to use sunlight to power satellites that will process data for AI and send the results back to Earth.

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Wednesday that the project, known as Starmind, will "support America's booming super intelligence economy".

Its approval comes as communities across the US have pushed back against the expansion of data centres on the ground.

Space X believes the "orbital data centres" are the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet the growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI) computing power that is beyond "terrestrial capabilities".

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement that the project "opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth".

"This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home," Carr said.

Responding to the announcement, Musk wrote on X: "Much appreciated. This will be a great asset to America and the world."

Gene Johnson, Associated Press Gene Johnson, Associated Press

Authorities are investigating why a small plane carrying six members of a Florida family crashed off the Mississippi coast on Tuesday. They were returning home from a fishing trip, relatives say.

The plane's pilot was Brent Stokes, the 50-year-old president of a marine contracting company based in Fort Myers, according to Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. Stokes' company's website described him as an "avid fisherman and life time boater."

The other victims were Stokes' 16-year-old son, Hunter Stokes; Stokes' sister, Arlyn Knox, 43; her husband, Michael Knox, 43; and their two sons, 12-year-old Charles Holden Knox and 10-year-old Truett Knox.

Arlyn and Michael Knox ran Knox Technologies, a Fort Myers-based IT company they founded in 2012, according to the company's website.

The Knox and Stokes families confirmed their deaths in an emailed statement provided to The Associated Press.

"They died doing what they loved: celebrating the start of a wonderful holiday season with a fishing trip together, before heading home to be with the rest of our family," the statement said. "In the middle of our grief, we are holding on to that, and to how much love they gave us and how much love surrounds us now. We will carry them with us always."

Lynd said that autopsies are being performed on Brent Stokes and Michael Knox, who was also a licensed pilot.

national.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to weather
national.summary: The was the first time ever that the iconic celebration - known for its massive balloons floating past the city's skyscrapers - was delayed because of storms.
national.body:
Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York to Saturday because of severe weather.

Preparations to hold the iconic holiday celebration, known for its massive balloons that float among the city's skyscrapers, had already begun when the forecast for heavy rain and strong winds on Thursday led to the delay.

The last time the parade was suspended was during World War Two, but it has never been postponed due to weather. In 1971, Macy's decided to ground the balloons, which often feature beloved characters from pop culture, because of weather.

A powerful coastal storm is set to affect the New York area in coming days.

The potent nor'easter storm is expected to make it too windy and dangerous for the iconic balloons to fly.

Macy's had expected to put 100 inflatables into the sky to mark its 100th parade and feature 10 new balloons, including one depicting the animated dog Bluey wearing a crown and another showing a Minion character riding a banana like a horse.

"While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants and spectators is, and always will be, our top priority," said Will Cross, the parade's executive producer, during a news conference on Wednesday with city officials.

Cross also said the giant balloons would be deflated on Wednesday night and stored at a facility in neighbouring New Jersey until they were reinflated for the parade on Saturday.

It was a sunny Wednesday afternoon on 26 November last year, and Mrs Lau was attending a dance class at an activity centre close to her home.

At around 14:45 she heard the faint sounds of fire engine sirens - but didn't think much of it.

It was only a while later, when she started receiving calls from a friend, that she found out that Wang Fuk Court - the eight-block apartment complex she had called home for the past 40 years - was ablaze. And her husband - a wheelchair user - was trapped inside their home.

"I grabbed my things quickly and ran down without even putting my shoes on properly," Mrs Lau, who wanted to be identified only by her surname, told the BBC.

When she got there, the building had been cordoned off by police.

She called her 74-year-old husband but he told her not to worry - he hadn't heard an alarm so it was probably a small fire, he said.

Mrs Lau could only watch helplessly as the blaze tore through Wang Fuk Court at a peak speed of about 10m (33ft) per second - an "unprecedented" rate, a final report released by an independent committee in relation to the deadly blaze that killed 168 people found.

It was a tragedy that was entirely preventable but happened as a result of a series of human errors, fire safety failures, alleged fraud and suspected corruption, said the report.

national.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle legal battle over French winery
national.summary: The Hollywood A-listers' legal battle focused on the vineyard they bought in 2008 and where they wed six years later.
national.body:
Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie have settled a long-running legal battle over her sale of a stake in their French vineyard, which unfolded amid a bitter divorce.

"We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further," said the Hollywood stars' representatives in a joint statement.

They bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008 and wed there six years later.

In the lawsuit, Pitt , 62, argued that Jolie , 51, acted without his permission in selling her share in the winery to a Russian oligarch. She counter-sued, accusing Pitt of drunkenly attacking her and their children on a flight, prompting her to file for divorce in 2016.

The settlement announced on Wednesday resolves both of their respective legal actions.

"Any comments in media stories attributed to 'sources' are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us," said the statement from their representatives.

Pitt's lawsuit had accused Jolie of seeking "to inflict harm" on him when she sold her stake in their co-owned vineyard, which he claimed had forced him to partner with "a stranger with poisonous associations and intentions".

The Fight Club star said he and Jolie had agreed not to sell their stakes in the venue without the permission of the other.

Becky Bohrer, Associated Press Becky Bohrer, Associated Press

JUNEAU, Alaska (AP) — A Republican official who oversees Alaska elections said she has ended an agreement under which the state shared its voter registration list with the U.S. Department of Justice and allowed the agency to flag voters for possible removal.

No voters were removed as a result of the agreement signed last December, and the Justice Department since then had not identified "any potentially ineligible voters or raised concerns regarding Alaska's voter registration records," the office of outgoing Lt. Gov. Nancy Dahlstrom said.

Dahlstrom said she notified the Justice Department that Alaska was terminating the agreement, effective Monday. That's also when Alaska officials announced that the results of the Nov. 3 general election, in which Democrats flipped a U.S. Senate seat and the governor's office, had been certified.

The Alaska Division of Elections directed the department to destroy the confidential voter information the state provided, Dahlstrom's office said in a statement released late Monday. A Justice Department spokesperson on Tuesday said the agency would send a formal response to the state.

The federal government's demand for detailed state voter information was part of a broader effort throughout the midterm election cycle to promote the idea that scores of noncitizens were on state voter rolls and potentially casting ballots illegally. In fact, years of research, state investigations and the Justice Department's own record of arrests showed the issue to be extremely rare.

The Justice Department sued 30 states and the District of Columbia for not complying with its demands to provide detailed voter registration data or other election-related records, with 28 of those lawsuits dismissed by courts, according to the Brennan Center for Justice. The department entered a settlement agreement with Oklahoma and dismissed its case with that state, the group said.

Alaska was one of at least 16 states to provide voter lists that included information such as driver's license and partial Social Security numbers, dates of birth and addresses. Alaska and Texas also signed data-sharing agreements with the Justice Department, in which it outlined plans for its own analysis of voter files, its plans to flag voter list issues and directions for removing voters deemed ineligible.

ATLANTA (AP) — A judge on Tuesday ordered Georgia's Fulton County to turn over a digital copy of ballots and other election records seized by the FBI earlier this year to the State Election Board, which had been trying for more than two years to obtain certain records from the 2020 election in the state's most populous county.

Fulton County Superior Court Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe ordered that the records be delivered to the state board by 5 p.m. Wednesday. She also put in place a protective order that limits who can see the unredacted records.

A Fulton County spokesperson declined to comment on a pending legal matter. The State Election Board did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.

The FBI served a search warrant at the Fulton County elections hub on Jan. 28 seeking records related to the 2020 election, leaving with hundreds of boxes containing ballots and other records. The county unsuccessfully sought to have a judge order the return of the records, but the federal government did provide the county with what it said was a digital copy of the records that were taken.

The overwhelmingly Democratic county, which includes most of the city of Atlanta, has been a target of President Donald Trump and his allies since he narrowly lost the presidential election in Georgia to Democrat Joe Biden in 2020. Trump has consistently insisted without evidence that widespread voter fraud in the county cost him victory in the state. Multiple courts and state and federal officials have found no evidence of fraud that would have altered the outcome.

A statement from an FBI agent supporting the search warrant used to take the records said the agency was examining possible "deficiencies or defects" in Fulton County's 2020 vote count. More than six years after that election and 10 months after the records seizure, no charges have been filed.

The FBI in July instructed field offices across the country to dedicate more than 200 staffers to its investigation of the 2020 election in Fulton County, describing it as a "priority investigation," and The New York Times reported that the FBI and federal prosecutors last week interviewed the man who served as the county's election director in 2020.

national.body:
Suman Naishadham, Associated Press Suman Naishadham, Associated Press

Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press Michael Kunzelman, Associated Press

MADRID (AP) — Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadoran national who fought his mistaken deportation from the United States, arrived in Spain on Wednesday after what his lawyer described as a temporary departure, with hopes of returning to his family's home in Maryland after President Donald Trump leaves office.

Ábrego García, who has an American wife and child, was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and was deported to a Salvadoran prison in what an official called an "administrative error." A judge later ordered his return to the U.S., where he fought the Trump administration's efforts to deport him again, this time to Africa.

After receiving officials' permission to leave the U.S., Ábrego García voluntarily departed on Tuesday from Washington Dulles International Airport, accompanied by his wife.

"The government does not decide where my story continues," the 31-year-old said during a virtual news conference Wednesday after he arrived in Spain. "My family and I will decide our future."

Simon Sandoval-Moshenberg, a Virginia-based attorney representing Ábrego García, called the move "a temporary departure," though he declined to say what his client's immediate plans are, including where he will live.

"Mr. Ábrego García has many options to return to the United States as the husband of a U.S. citizen spouse and the father of a U.S. citizen child. We don't expect that to happen under this administration, which we know will never give him a fair shake, but we expect that the next administration will prioritize reunifying this family and bringing him back to Maryland," Sandoval-Moshenberg said.

national.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
national.summary: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.
national.body:
Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says.

Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening.

Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched.

Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

The regional public prosecutor has launched an investigation into the incident and asked that DNA samples be taken from bodies of the dead.

The tanker, which belonged to a private contractor, had been travelling along the highway when a high-voltage cable fell in front of it, prompting the driver to lose control, Al-Ahram reports, citing sources with knowledge of the investigation.

It then crossed the central reservation, overturned and caught fire, the state-owned newspaper says.

Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years, with informal residential areas and often run-down infrastructure making incidents more common, the response to which is often complicated by slow emergency response times and locally improvised rescue efforts, even in the sprawling Egyptian capital.

national.title: These young Republicans have a message for their party: It's time to 'grow up'
national.summary: Three weeks after midterm elections that devastated the Republican Party, several dozen of its more youthful members gathered at a brewery to sort through the pieces.
national.body:
Jesse Bedayn, Associated Press Jesse Bedayn, Associated Press

FORT WORTH, Texas (AP) — Three weeks after midterm elections that devastated the Republican Party, several dozen of its more youthful members gathered at a brewery to sort through the pieces.

The Monday meeting was organized by the Tarrant County Young Republicans, a local organization on the front lines of a national reckoning. Their last leader resigned shortly before the midterms because she couldn't bring herself to vote for some of her party's candidates. Then their county, once a conservative stronghold, flipped blue.

"Everyone has someone to blame, and that finger is never pointed at ourself," said Derrick Wilson, who heads the Texas Young Republican Federation, a coalition that includes the Tarrant County chapter. "So we're going to have to get past that and figure out, what did we do wrong?"

WATCH: How the Latino shift to Democrats helped turn Texas blue

Democrats won the U.S. Senate race and the governor's office in Texas, their first statewide victories in over three decades. There's no consensus about the path forward, but several people at this week's meeting gave similar answers.

Some are bored with "owning the libs" and put off by meme-driven political messaging that they see as flippant in the face of real challenges. Many felt President Donald Trump didn't follow through on his promises. And others gave similar advice to their party leaders: "grow up," "take themselves seriously" and "be humble."

The event opened with someone introduced by Wilson as a "survivor" of the midterms. State Appeals Court Judge Brian Walker, a Republican who won reelection, gave a withering assessment of how the party had stumbled down the wrong path with Trump-style belligerent politics led by the "loudest" and "craziest" voices.

national.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row
national.summary: Swiss officials said relations would be kept through North Korea's embassy in Bern, and its own embassy in Beijing.
national.body:
North Korea has ordered Switzerland's diplomatic representative to leave the country within 48 hours and called for the office to close, in a row over sanctions.

It followed Switzerland's decision to place sanctions on the Songdowon international children's camp in the eastern city of Wonsan, which is attended by Russian and Chinese children among other nationalities.

The camp has been accused of involvement in transferring children from Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine.

North Korea's state-run news agency KCNA called the sanctions "a blatant hostile act".

Switzerland is one of the few Western nations to maintain dialogue with Pyongyang.

Confirming the expulsion, KCNA said: "The Foreign Ministry of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) declared the head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours."

The diplomatic rebuke comes weeks after Swiss foreign minister Ignazio Cassis made a rare visit to North Korea, where he officially reopened the office and discussed normalising relations.

Swiss authorities said relations between the two countries would be maintained through the North Korean embassy in Bern, and the Swiss embassy in Beijing.

local.body: Small businesses along Buffalo's Elmwood Avenue are gearing up for what they hope will be a big weekend for local shopping.Small Business Saturday is this weekend, serving as a community-driven counterpoint to the retail push of Black Friday.I spoke with several Elmwood Village business owners. Tracey Wei, who owns zero-waste home and body care store Little Salmon, described the area as "welcoming and walkable."Wei told me independent businesses like hers often rely on Small Business Saturday to stay afloat."This weekend is like make-or-break for the last quarter," Wei said.Like many businesses in the neighborhood, she'll be holding a sale on Saturday to promote more foot traffic."Businesses need your money more than billionaires, so every dollar you spend, like 70-80% of it stays with the community," she said.WATCH: 'Make-or-break': Buffalo businesses prepare for Small Business SaturdayOther owners pointed to the unique experience shoppers find in the neighborhood."There are many unique shops you're not gonna find somewhere else, and you get better customer service," Wendie Reed said.At Reed's consignment store, Scoop Shop, shoppers might even find an outfit for the World's Largest Disco on Saturday at the Buffalo Convention Center.Small Business Saturday is one of many events being held to bring people to the area. Seamus Gallivan, the new executive director of the Elmwood Village Association, said the density of the neighborhood is part of its appeal."The beautiful thing about this neighborhood is there are so many businesses so close together that however you get here, you can stay on foot for hours and find everything you need and more," Gallivan explained. He said the stores will also participate in a Christmas window display competition starting December 5. For now, the focus is on bringing people out this Saturday. local.summary: WESTFIELD — A Portland resident is facing charges after he allegedly spray-painted and attempted to drill a hole into the Lincoln statue in the village. local.body:
WESTFIELD — A Portland resident is facing charges after he allegedly spray-painted and attempted to drill a hole into the Lincoln statue in the village.

At approximately 2:42 p.m. Wednesday, the Westfield Police Department responded to a criminal mischief complaint at Main and Portage streets. A male wearing a flannel shirt, later identified as Nicholas A. Rychick, was spray-painting and attempting to drill a hole into the bronze statue of Abraham Lincoln. A bystander confronted Rychick, 37, who fled in a vehicle.

With assistance from the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office and New York State Police, officers located Rychick and his vehicle at a residence in Portland. He was taken into custody without incident and transported to WPD.

The investigation determined that Rychick allegedly attempted to drill a hole into the chest of the memorial to place an arrow into the statue but was unsuccessful. He allegedly proceeded to spray-paint the memorial, damaging it and surrounding holiday decorations.

Rychick was arrested on the above charges, processed and released on appearance tickets directing him to appear before the Town of Westfield Court at a later date.

The Westfield Police Department thanks the concerned citizen who intervened, the Chautauqua County Sheriff's Office and the New York State Police for their assistance.

The statue, which was erected in 1999, showcases unique, bronze statues of Lincoln and Grace Bedell, the girl who suggested that he grow a beard for his presidential campaign.

Grace Bedell, a young girl from Westfield wrote a letter to Mr. Abraham Lincoln, Presidential Candidate, in 1860, encouraging him to “grow whiskers and her brothers would vote for him and he would look nicer.”

local.title: Brighton preparing for first phase of its Multiversity Trail project
local.summary: The town is focusing on a stretch of the Lehigh Valley Trail that will be part of the network.
local.body:
The town of Brighton has received a $1.4 million grant from the state to improve a section of the Lehigh Valley Trail between the University of Rochester and Rochester Institute of Technology.

The work is part of the town's Multiversity Trail effort that aims to link the university, RIT, and Monroe Community College campuses using the Lehigh Valley Trail and the Erie Canalway Trail. On the Lehigh Valley Trail leg, the town plans to replace most of the surface, among other things.

"It's an old rail trail, the old Lehigh Valley train line, but you know it really needs upgrading, accessibility, signage, drainage issues," Brighton Supervisor Bill Moehle said. "So we'll be able to address all of those and more with this grant."

Moehle added that the town also wants to install flashing beacons at major road crossings that trail users would be able to activate, similar to the Auburn Trail.

Local News Brighton wants to connect bike trails for students at 3 campuses Jeremy Moule The town has three colleges within and along its borders. It wants students at them to be able to easily bike between campuses. The Lehigh Valley Trail work marks the first phase of the Multiversity Trail project. The town plans to put out a request for proposals around design work early next year.

Moehle said the project will benefit more than the college communities. The Lehigh trail is well used, he said, and an important connector for people living on the west side of town.

"It'll focus on the connection between the U of R and RIT because, you know, we have something there to work with," Moehle said. "There is an existing trail, and this will make it really much more user friendly for all users."

local.title: State announces increased road patrols during holiday weekend
local.summary: Motorists heading out for the holiday are being urged to play it safe. On Wednesday, state Gov. Kathy Hochul announced State Police and local law enforcement agencies statewide will increase patrols to target impaired and reckless driving during the Thanksgiving travel season. Funded by the Governor
local.body:
Motorists heading out for the holiday are being urged to play it safe.

On Wednesday, state Gov. Kathy Hochul announced State Police and local law enforcement agencies statewide will increase patrols to target impaired and reckless driving during the Thanksgiving travel season. Funded by the Governor's Traffic Safety Committee (GTSC), the impaired driving enforcement mobilization will run through Sunday.

"As we gather with friends and family to celebrate Thanksgiving, I want to ensure that everyone gets where they are going safely and not have what should be happy memories marred by a preventable tragedy," Hochul said. "I urge drivers to stay alert, stay sober and move over when you see vehicles stopped on the side of the road. If you're in a vehicle, you should wear seat belts or use proper restraint. I thank our law enforcement for sacrificing their time with loved ones to work on Thanksgiving and throughout the holidays to help keep New York's roadways safe."

In addition to increased traffic volume, the Thanksgiving holiday period is also associated with increased alcohol use. During the 2025 Thanksgiving holiday period, law enforcement officers arrested 2,236 drivers for driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs, 12,496 for speeding and also issued 3,075 tickets to unbelted drivers and passengers.

New York State Police Superintendent Steven G. James said, "Our members work vigilantly year-round to keep our roadways safe and prevent the needless tragedies that result from impaired and reckless driving. As always, we will be doing our part to ensure the holidays are safe for all who live in and travel through our great state. Please think twice before getting behind the wheel of a vehicle if you've been drinking. If you have had alcohol, there are several options available that will provide you with a safe ride to your destination. Together, let's make safety a top priority on our roadways this holiday season."

The State Police will supplement regular patrols statewide through efforts including fixed sobriety checkpoints and utilizing Concealed Identity Traffic Enforcement (CITE) patrol vehicles to better spot distracted drivers and those talking or texting on handheld devices. These unmarked vehicles blend in with everyday traffic but are unmistakable as emergency vehicles once the emergency lighting is activated.

Mtorists must follow the state's Move Over law, which was expanded in March 2024 to require drivers to slow down and move over for all vehicles stopped along the roadway if they can safely do so. The Thruway Authority and state Department of Transportation urge motorists to stay alert while driving, slow down and safely move over when they see a vehicle on the side of the road. The lives of motorists, employees, roadway workers and emergency personnel depend on it.

entertainment.body:
Alan Bersten deserves the Mirrorball for best backup dancer.

The Dancing With the Stars pro proved he was Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach ’s secret weapon during the Nov. 24 finale while performing during their freestyle routine to Linkin’ Park ’s “Numb.” When the Paralympian’s prosthetic leg accidentally fell off mid-show, Bersten quickly grabbed the device and held it for safekeeping until Karagach could give it to Frech to reattach during the song. Plus, Bersten was locked into the choreography and didn’t even miss his cue to tear off Frech’s rip-away clothing.

Following Frech and Karagach’s win, Bersten shared how honored he was to have taken part in the dance alongside the duo.

“I just want to take a second and congratulate Ezra and Daniella,” he said in a Nov. 25 TikTok . “Ezra, your resilience and your composure and your courage is so inspiring.”

The 32-year-old— who was eliminated during week two alongside pro partner Giada De Laurentiis —added that the moment Frech reattached his leg mid-dance was one that “transcends Dancing with the Stars .”

“It's a moment that will live on forever,” he said. “And I hope you are so proud of yourself, Daniella. You've created something so magical. Congratulations, you guys.”

Karagach thanked her fellow pro for not only grabbing the prosthetic when it fell, but also for clearing away Frech’s tearaway suit from the stage so it wouldn’t get in their way.

“The way @alanbersten slid me that leg and made sure Ezra's rip away was cleared was true professionalism at its finest,” the 33-year-old posted to her Instagram Stories Nov. 24. “Grateful you had our backs. Can't thank you enough.”

entertainment.title: FCC Bid Challenging ABC’s TV Licenses Halted in Major Win for Network
entertainment.summary: The ruling is a major setback for the administration in the government's campaign against ABC and national media.
entertainment.body:
Logo text ABC has won a court order barring the Federal Communications Commission from taking further action against the network amid the government’s efforts to possibly strip the company of its local broadcast licenses.

U.S. District Judge Loren Alikhan on Wednesday rebuffed the FCC ‘s bid to dismiss the lawsuit, finding that the agency likely violated ABC’s First Amendment rights by weaponizing its regulatory authority to retaliate against the network for protected speech and pressure it to change its editorial decisions.

The Disney-owned company sued the FCC earlier this year after the Brendan Carr-led agency called for an early review of ABC’s broadcast licenses. The renewal prompted concerns of retaliation since it followed an investigation into Disney’s diversity practices and ABC late-night host Kimmy Kimmel angering President Donald Trump with a joke. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: 'Dancing With the Stars' Records Another Huge Finale TV 'Dancing With the Stars' Names Historic Season 35 Winner: See All the Scores, Who Won

In Wednesday’s ruling, the court said that Carr’s conduct is “powerful evidence” of the FCC’s “retaliatory motive.”

“It is no coincidence that President Trump criticized Mr. Kimmel’s skit on social media and the very next day Defendants initiated the early license renewal proceedings,” Alikhan wrote. She pointed to Carr’s comment that “we can do this the easy way or the hard way” and that “these companies can find ways to take action on Kimmel, or there is going to be additional work for the FCC ahead.”

The FCC has maintained that the early license renewal proceedings are merely “in aid” of its investigation into Disney’s employment practices and would’ve occurred regardless.

The court was unconvinced, finding that it “does not find that explanation to be credible.” It stressed that Trump has targeted ABC for several years.

The FCC has also launched a separate inquiry into The View , which it argued is not a “bona fide” news program and therefore is not exempt from FCC equal opportunity rules. This came after an appearance by James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for the Texas Senate, in February. ABC said in an earlier filing that the FCC “now appears poised to find that The View must provide equal opportunities to all legally qualified political candidates if it interviews one candidate on the show, which would represent a reversal of decades of agency precedent.”

entertainment.title: How The One Ring Helps Sauron Control The Other Rings Of Power
entertainment.summary: "The Rings of Power" season 3 finale shows but a glimpse of the One Ring's immense power, leaving us with a lot to look forward to in season 4.
entertainment.body:
New Line Cinema Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 8 – "The Doom of Men"

"The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 8 sees Sauron finally wielding his One Ring of power — that is, until he takes it off and surrenders to his enemies. Don't worry, there's more to that move than the Dark Lord willingly giving up. He'll be back. When Sauron first forges the One Ring at the end of Episode 7 , he puts it on, and the Elven ring-bearers immediately remove their own overpowered jewelry. They're aware of the Dark Lord, and they don't want to be controlled by him. But what exactly does the One Ring do to allow the Dark Lord to control the other Rings of Power?

Tolkien doesn't give a clear, scientific answer here. But in "The Silmarillion" he does provide a good summary: "Now the Elves made many rings; but secretly Sauron made One Ring to rule all the others, and their power was bound up with it, to be subject wholly to it and to last only so long as it too should last." The book explains that Sauron pours much of his own strength and will into his Ring so it can control the others, saying, "while he wore the One Ring, he could perceive all the things that were done by means of the lesser rings, and he could see and govern the very thoughts of those that wore them."

Prime Video The One Ring rules the others. There's no doubt about that. In a letter to a publisher in 1951, Tolkien clarified the power of the One Ring over other rings, adding to the description that, along with containing all of the powers of the other Rings, it could see the thoughts and govern their behavior "and in the end could utterly enslave them."

However, the way the One Ring controls the wearers of the "lesser rings" of power isn't consistent. A lot of this depends on who's wearing them. The Elves, for instance, are instantly aware of Sauron when he puts on the One Ring. They're able to understand what's happening and have the willpower to take off their Rings and hide them.

In contrast, the Nine Rings for Mortal Men give Sauron complete control over their owners. "The Silmarillion" says, "They fell under the thraldom of the ring that they bore and under the domination of the One, which was Sauron's." Even when Sauron doesn't have the One Ring, he still has a degree of slavish control over these Men. (What's Elrond's line again? Men are weak.)

entertainment.title: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie Settle Bitter Winery War That Detailed Abuse Claims
entertainment.summary: The nearly six-year legal battle involved allegations Pitt was abusive and wanted Jolie to sign a non-disparagement agreement
entertainment.body:
When Brad Pitt first sued Angelina Jolie in 2022, he accused his ex-wife of unlawfully going behind his back to sell her stake in Château Miraval, the former couple’s prized winery in the south of France.

Jolie responded with a countersuit in October 2022, saying she had done “everything within her control” to make their business partnership work, only to have Pitt seize creative control and overrule her on extravagant projects, allegedly including a fifth swimming pool costing one million euros.

She then raised the stakes considerably, claiming Pitt had turned “physically and emotionally abusive” toward her and their children during an outburst on a private plane in 2016 that led to the collapse of their marriage. Jolie said she initially considered selling her stake in Miraval to Pitt, realizing it would eventually go to their children, but the deal fell apart when Pitt allegedly demanded a non-disparagement clause she blasted as an “unconscionable gag order.”

On Wednesday, the former Hollywood power couple announced they reached a private settlement in their nearly five-year legal war, heading off a public and potentially bruising trial set for next August.

That's what Cora (Hunter Schafer) tells Elias (Lewis Gribben) in the penultimate episode of "Blade Runner 2099." The revelation that their adopted mother Helena (Sheila Atim) was actually a replicant — one of the two original Nexus-1 models — shakes Cora to her foundation, and it's the twist through which the show frames its central ideas of what it means to be human. Those questions of passing and authenticity, of whether the differences inherent to replicants are even real, echo even louder through the show's final episode, in which both Cora and Olwen face their humanity in fascinating ways.

Episode 7 ends with Julius (Tom Burke) — the last living Nexus-1 — bombing the replicants' Los Angeles birthing center and making off with the genetic blueprint for his original model. Back at his makeshift lab, he successfully uses the heisted data to extend the life of his partner, Clotilde (Amy Lennox), killing her and rewriting her genetic code to bring her back to life with renewed longevity. Cora and Olwen leave the city in search of them, both desperate to claim the Tyrell memory, and its implications, for themselves.

Throughout its eight episodes, "2099" has shown that its writers understand what "Blade Runner" has always been about: loneliness, empathy, selfishness, love, and the way these forces tangle together to form the inscrutable motivations we identify as human. In its grand finale, "2099" yanks on that knot of emotional strands, leaving some big questions in the best of ways.

In a moment, we'll want to hear what you thought of the final episode. First, let's get into it.

entertainment.title: Duran Duran’s Biggest Billboard Hits: ‘Rio,’ ‘Hungry Like the Wolf’ & More

entertainment.body:
Duran Duran charted 15 hits in the top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100 in 1983-93, a run of synth-pop classics, boosted by stylish videos amid MTV’s most tastemaking era, that led to the band ranking among the 100 top-performing acts in the chart’s history.

After John Taylor and Nick Rhodes formed the group in Birmingham, England, in 1978, Duran Duran — by then rounded out by lead singer Simon LeBon, Andy Taylor and Roger Taylor (with none of the Taylors related) — made its Hot 100 debut on Christmas Day 1982 with “Hungry Like the Wolf.” The following March, the single became the group’s first of 11 top 10s, reaching No. 3.

After “Rio” hit No. 14 in May 1983, two more Hot 100 top 10s followed that year: “Is There Something I Should Know” and “Union of the Snake.”

Duran Duran scored its first Hot 100 No. 1, “The Reflex,” in 1984 and added its second, “A View to a Kill,” in 1985, the latter marking the only leader on the list ever from the James Bond film franchise.

Later in the ‘80s, Duran Duran continued to scale the Hot 100’s top 10, while members posted hits via their own ventures, with Andy Taylor joining supergroup Power Station , which scored two top 10s in 1985: “Some Like It Hot” (No. 6) and “Get It On (Bang a Gong)” (No. 9).

Plus, Andy Taylor — who, as announced Nov. 25, died at age 65 — reached No. 24 in 1986 with his solo song “Take It Easy.”

Meanwhile, Arcadia — LeBon, Rhodes and Roger Taylor — notched two top 40 Hot 100 hits in 1985-86, led by the No. 6-peaking “Election Day.”

In 1993, Duran Duran (then comprising LeBon, Rhodes, John Taylor and Warren Cuccurullo), upped its count to 10 and 11 top 10s thanks to “Ordinary World” and “Come Undone.”

entertainment.body:
Aaron Rodgers ' relationship with his coach entered the red zone.

The Pittsburgh Steelers player did not hold back about his opinion of coach Mike McCarthy after learning that he would be punting the title of starting quarterback. Rodgers lashed out at the NFL coach for surprisingly benching him for the NFL season—in favor of teammate Mason Rudolph —and has since been cut from the team.

"Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, that word never even came up," Rodgers revealed on Nov. 25 episode of The Pat McAfee Show , referring to "benching." He added that on a phone call with other team leadership he heard, "'I can't believe they're doing this,'" prompting him to ask, "'Doing what?' I didn't know."

And the former Green Bay Packer—who first worked with McCarthy for over a decade in Wisconsin—didn't toe the line when it came to detailing his issues with the 63-year-old, including a claim that McCarthy fell asleep during meetings.

"We were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down and within 10 minutes began snoring," Rodgers, 42, recounted. "Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened."

Rodgers shared that his position stemmed from being "a concerned friend about somebody who's unhealthy. If you're sleeping in meetings, you're unhealthy," adding that McCarthy was "not coming to everything you should be coming to as a play caller."

That said, the Cal alum also stated McCarthy even missed meetings ahead of game day, such as before the Steelers' tough loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22.

And given Rodgers' concerns, he initiated a conversation about changes he believed were mandatory to move forward. In his words, he told McCarthy days before being deemed inactive, "'We got to make a change, like for the betterment of the team.’"

entertainment.title: ‘Twilight’ Director Reveals Robert Pattinson Inspired James Bond Line in 2008 Film: “We Were Seeing the Future”
entertainment.summary: Earlier this month, it was announced that Pattinson has been tapped as the new 007, succeeding Daniel Craig.
entertainment.body:
Catherine Hardwicke , who helmed 2008’s Twilight , might as well have had a crystal ball on the set of the vampire romance film.

After it was revealed earlier this month that Robert Pattinson — who earned his breakout role as Edward Cullen in the blockbuster franchise — had been tapped as the new James Bond , fans were quick to point out that Twilight predicted his 007 casting nearly two decades ago.

At one point in the movie, Eric’s (played by Justin Chon) discusses the prom theme and says, “Gambling, tuxedos, and Bond, James Bond ,” right before the camera cuts to a smirking Edward, looking suave in a pair of sunglasses. Related Stories Movies Prince Harry Approves of Robert Pattinson's Bond Casting Movies The Time Robert Pattinson Snuck Around Rikers Island (and Why It Could Help Him With James Bond)

In a recent interview on The Kyle Buchanan Show , Hardwicke recalled how that line and scene came about. “You guys have probably seen online where we have that [ Twilight ] scene where he [Eric] says, ‘Bond, James Bond,’ and then we cut to Rob,” she said. “That’s the one scene where I was like, ‘Let’s put the sunglasses on that day,’ and he got out of the car and he looked so suave that he inspired the line, ‘Bond, James Bond.’

The director added that Chon “kind of ad-libbed it, and it was kind of cool because we did think he looked like James Bond. So I guess we were seeing the future.”

Fast forward to 2026 and Denis Villeneuve, who’s helming the new 007 movie, and producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman, obviously thought Pattinson looked like Bond too . The Primetime actor is taking over the iconic role from Daniel Craig, who concluded his run with 2021’s No Time to Die .

Hardwicke also shared her reaction to the news that Pattinson would be going from having “the skin of a killer” to getting his license to kill.

“I almost fell out of my bed,” she quipped about the moment she learned about the casting. “I just didn’t think they were going to choose him because of The Batman and he’s so famous and they like to get the unknown [actor]. So I did almost fall out of the bed, and that is the same bed that Rob and Kristen [Stewart, who played Bella Swan in Twilight ] auditioned for the first time and did their kissing scene. So it was kind of bizarre. And he [Pattinson] fell out of the bed when he did the audition and landed on the floor, so it was kind of cool.”

The ongoing legal battle between Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie has finally come to an end.

The Ocean’s Eleven actor and Maleficent star have settled their years-long dispute over the sale of their French winery, Chateau Miraval, which they purchased in 2008 and was the location of their 2014 wedding.

“We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” reps for Jolie and Pitt said in a Nov. 25 statement to E! News. “Any comments in media stories attributed to ‘sources’ are in fact not coming from either of us, or anyone close to us.”

The former couple’s legal woes began in 2022 when Pitt sued Jolie for allegedly selling her interests in their once-shared French estate, according to court documents obtained by E! News at the time.

The Bullet Train actor said in the docs that he had a "mutual and binding commitment" with Jolie that neither one of them would sell their shares to a third party without the other's consent. However, according to the lawsuit, Pitt learned in October 2021 that Tenute del Mondo, a company with ties to Russian billionaire Yuri Shefler , had allegedly bought Jolie's shares of Miraval.

Jolie then filed a $250 million countersuit against Pitt in September of that year, alleging he devised a campaign to "seize control" of the once-shared estate after their 2016 split. This lawsuit, obtained by E! News at the time, alleged that Jolie only sold her portion of the estate to an outside company when Pitt refused to remove the NDA stipulations he'd included as part of the deal.

The legal saga got even more intense when Jolie accused Pitt of abuse in a cross complaint obtained by E! News in October 2022 . In the court docs, Jolie addressed a 2016 airplane incident that allegedly occurred days before she decided to file for divorce , in which she alleged that Pitt had choked one of their children.

More allegations came out in April 2024 when Jolie filed documents stating, “While Pitt's history of physical abuse of Jolie started well before the family's September 2016 plane trip from France to Los Angeles, this flight marked the first time he turned his physical abuse on the children as well. entertainment.body:
If your Turkey Day plans include watching the parade, be prepared for some deflating news.

The annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in history, with the milestone 100th celebration being delayed two days until Nov. 28 due to a severe storm headed to New York City, an NBC spokesperson confirmed to E! News.

“Due to the extreme weather conditions, the city of New York, Macy’s and NBC have decided,” the spokesperson shared in a Nov. 25 statement, “in the interest of safety for both the participants and spectators, to move the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, Nov. 28. More details to follow.”

Macy’s expressed gratitude for the many people who bring the parade to living rooms every Thanksgiving.

“Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year,” a spokesperson told MSNOW in a statement. “We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.”

And while the announcement marks the first time the parade has been postponed since its debut in 1924, the Thanksgiving Day staple has been cancelled three times throughout its 100-year history—from 1942 to 1944—due to World War II.

This year, the monumental centennial celebration was set to take place on Thursday, when a coastal storm is predicted the Big Apple and eastern coastline, bringing rain and strong winds.

This poses a major safety concern not only for the millions of New Yorkers who watch the parade in person, but also for the thousands of performers who participate, alongside the nearly 30 floats and record-breaking 100 inflatables , which will include characters such as Bluey, Buckaroo Bob the Minion and Hello Kitty.

entertainment.title: ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ Producer Alex Gayner Thought He’d Solved Every Problem a Set Could Throw at Him. Then Came a Runaway Parrot.
entertainment.summary: Ten seconds of footage ended up being the most nerve-wracking part of the shoot for the movie veteran who has been on sets since the '90s.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Filmmakers often thrive on controlled chaos. Alex Gayner has spent his career orchestrating that madness.

Long before producing The Mosquito Bowl for Peter Berg , Gayner cut his teeth doing odd jobs on ’90s direct-to-video actioners — the kind of movies you’d stumble across on a pay-cable channel at 1 AM during a bout of insomnia. Then, a second assistant director was let go before lunch, and Gayner found himself promoted on the spot. It was an unlikely break that set the course for the rest of his career.

He gradually climbed the ranks to first assistant director, eventually trading B-movies for some of the biggest studio productions around, including Guillermo del Toro’s Pacific Rim and Gareth Edwards’ Godzilla . He also developed a reputation as a closer, overseeing reshoots for Suicide Squad (2016), Birds of Prey , Zero Dark Thirty and Mulan , among others. Related Stories TV 'Beef' Creator Lee Sung Jin Launches Production Company, Plans Ali Wong Limited Series Movies Ray Nicholson Levels Up With 'The Mosquito Bowl': "I'm Always Battling for Legitimacy"

Another turning point arrived in the late 2010s, when the native New Yorker decided to pivot to producing. If the first AD is the on-set quarterback who executes the plays on the field, then Gayner wanted to become a full-time offensive coordinator, the person drawing up the plays and mapping out the production behind the scenes.

He credits Nicolas Winding Refn with giving him his big break as a producer on the 2019 limited series Too Old to Die Young , an opportunity that paved the way for him to produce the first season of Beef and win an Emmy for his work. (Gayner and Refn are now assembling the latter’s long-gestating Maniac Cop reimagining, which recently received approval for a California tax credit.)

After wrapping Beef , Netflix pointed Gayner toward Berg’s 19th-century Western limited series American Primeval . But first, the two had to bridge the gap between the producer Berg expected and the one Gayner turned out to be.

“When I met Pete, I don’t think he really knew what kind of producer I was,” Gayner tells The Hollywood Reporter . “Naturally, he didn’t know if I was going to come in to watch the money or try to make the show on soundstages. We had to figure each other out.”

To keep the football metaphors going, Berg likes to run his sets with a no-huddle offense, frequently calling audibles along the way. He might improvise dialogue, change camera positions or throw out the playbook altogether. Most of all, he has a strict devotion to immersive, practical filmmaking. Fortunately, Gayner has been adapting on the fly ever since that lunchtime promotion more than 30 years ago. He also shares Berg’s preference for capturing as much as possible in camera.

entertainment.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers cut the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player on Wednesday, shortly after he torched Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on ESPN’s The Pat McAfee Show .

The move capped a chaotic 18 hours in which the team announced it was benching the 42-year-old future Hall of Famer for backup Mason Rudolph ahead of Friday’s visit from Denver. Related Stories Business Tony Romo Lands Post-CBS Gig With Betting App Betr as "Chief Predictions Officer" (Exclusive) TV Tom Jackson, Denver Broncos' All-Pro Linebacker and ESPN Analyst, Dies at 75

Rodgers responded by taking an excused absence from the club, then used the unexpected time off to go on McAfee and repeatedly call the 62-year-old McCarthy’s mental state into question.

Rodgers told McAfee he found out about the surprise decision while on the phone with teammates, including tight end Pat Freiermuth.

It was just the start of a blistering offensive from Rodgers, who painted McCarthy — whom he played under during a long successful run in Green Bay earlier in their careers — as a leader woefully out of touch.

He described a quarterback meeting last Wednesday with McCarthy arriving late, sat down “and within 10 minutes began snoring,” woke up and nodded off again minutes later, then eventually “walks out of the room like nothing happened.” Rodgers also said McCarthy missed an offensive meeting Thursday, missed a walkthrough Friday and a morning meeting Saturday while not holding a team meeting that night.

“And then comes to Sunday, when obviously we struggled and the product wasn’t great,” Rodgers said, adding that McCarthy broke up the halftime locker room meeting by saying “1-2-3 Packers.”

Rodgers said he felt it was the right thing to bring up the issues to McCarthy as a longtime league star instead of putting it on others with fewer years, shaky roster positions or those who “haven’t made $400 million dollars in the NFL.”

entertainment.title: King Crimson Co-Founder Michael Giles Dead at 84
entertainment.summary: As part of Giles, Giles, and Fripp, he'd laid the sound that would change prog rock forever when he helpd form King Crimson to record In the Court of the Crimson King
entertainment.body:
Michael Giles, a drummer and singer who cofounded King Crimson , died Monday, according to King Crimson’s record label, DGM , which did not report a cause of death. Giles was 84.

“Michael’s originality, musical curiosity and uncompromising commitment to creative freedom challenged conventions and inspired generations of musicians around the world,” Crimson’s label said. “He leaves behind an extraordinary musical legacy, and his unique contribution to the evolution of progressive music will never be forgotten.”

Giles’ musical beginnings with Giles, Giles, and Fripp, a trio he cofounded in 1967 in Bournemouth — where was he was born on March 1, 1942 — with his brother Peter and guitarist Robert Fripp, were inauspicious, at least by King Crimson standards. The band’s only album, 1968’s The Cheerful Insanity of Giles, Giles and Fripp , was all psychedelia: shimmering organ, pensive vocals, and relatively straightforward, march-like drumming that only occasionally hinted at jazziness. It’s straightforward pop rock, but you can also hear how it provided the framework for King Crimson’s outré, ponderous adventures a year later.

When Peter quit to become a solicitor’s clerk in November 1968, Michael and Fripp wanted to continue making music, so they formed King Crimson with Greg Lake, who’d played bass with the Gods, and multi-instrumentalist Ian McDonald. The lineup included Peter Sinfield as lyricist and lighting director. Together, the conceived an album that would define the sound of prog rock in the early Seventies: In the Court of the Crimson King , which came out in 1969.

The album’s seven-minute opening cut, “21st Century Schizoid Man,” was an FM radio hit in spite of its turn-on-a-dime rhythm changes and extended bass and sax duets. The stylistic shift allowed Giles to challenge himself to make his drum parts more musical, whether mirroring McDonald’s sax or rolling rhythms like waves in the main riff. “The Court of the Crimson King,” a 10-minute musical journey, took the streamlined rock sound of Giles, Giles, and Fripp and augmented it with flute, Mellotron, and choral-like harmonies. Giles’ drumming on the song is the musical equivalent to expressionism as he brings out his bandmates’ drama. He latter cited Elvin Jones, who’d played with John Coltrane, as an inspiration. Ferrell and Netflix are not done with each other, however: Ferrell is executive producing new Netflix series All the Rage , Prep , and Nikki Glaser’s first (unnamed) scripted series. (Part of her Netflix Is a Joke Studios deal.) Ferrell produces for his Gloria Sanchez banner.

The problem with The Hawk was, well, it was (very) subpar . The Hawk , co-created by Ferrell and Harper Steele, followed disgraced pro golfer Lonnie Hawkins (Ferrell) who seeks to regain his former glory. Molly Shannon played Ferrell’s wife and Jimmy Tatro placed their son Lance. Related Stories Movies Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. It Was Actually David Fincher Wanting Him in 'Cliff Booth' TV 'The Body' Star Kristina Bogic Just Wanted to Take Care of Anya: "A Lot of Young Women Can Relate"

In his review , THR TV critic Daniel Fienberg called The Hawk “disposable,” writing that, “In general, The Hawk is a show that consistently operates at a barely minimal level, starting with the credits song, a slice of ’80s anthemic rock that contains the lyrics, ‘They call him the Hawk/ He’s a golfer/ The greatest golfer in the world.’ Wait. Sorry. The song doesn’t contain those lyrics — those are the only lyrics. It’s a piece of cheeky minimalism and a promise delivered.”

“There will be countless worse shows this year, but it’s doubtful that 2026 will offer a show as hollow and forgettable as The Hawk ,” Fienberg scathed.

In addition to Ferrell and Steele, Jessica Elbaum, Alix Taylor, Rian Johnson, Ram Bergman, Nena Rodrigue, Chris Henchy, David Gordon Green and Andrew Guest also executive produced The Hawk .
